mechanisms.text: Grading is performed by judge_eq, which takes the gold answer option, the model's raw output, the question prompt, and the OpenAI client (suggesting LLM-as-judge for ambiguous cases); it returns a (result, is_ambiguous) tuple.
Three TV-show scripts are supported as separate evaluation targets: Friends, The Big Bang Theory, and The Office, with a named chatbot character per script.
Experiments are run three times (due to randomized question selection per run) and accuracy with standard deviation is reported.
Retrieval methods include BM25, OpenAI embeddings, no retrieval, and oracle retrieval.

ledger.claim: GPT-4o-mini is used as the LLM judge for multi_choice_unstructured and open_ended answer formats.
ledger.quote: we use gpt-4o-mini as a judge when answer_format is "multi_choice_unstructured" or "open_ended"
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Oracle retrieval is available as a setting, providing an upper-bound retrieval condition.
ledger.quote: Options include "openai-emb", "bm25", "no_ret", and "oracle".

ledger.claim: The number of retrieved history segments is configurable and requires modifying simulator.py lines 180-198 and 222-236.

ledger.claim: DialSim evaluates three TV-show scripts: Friends (chatbot=Ross), The Big Bang Theory (chatbot=Sheldon), The Office (chatbot=Michael).

ledger.claim: Evaluated agents include state-of-the-art LLM-based conversational agents with large context windows or RAG capabilities.
ledger.quote: Our evaluation of state-of-the-art LLM-based conversational agents using DialSim reveals that even models with large context windows or RAG capabilities struggle
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: The benchmark was submitted June 2024 and revised through September 2025 (v6).
ledger.quote: [v1] Wed, 19 Jun 2024 … [v6] Fri, 26 Sep 2025
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Primary metric is accuracy (CorrectAnswers / TotalQuestions) computed over randomly sampled questions across sessions.
ledger.quote: CorrectAnswers / TotalQuestions
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Experiments are run three times per condition; accuracy and standard deviation are reported.
ledger.quote: We conducted experiments three times and reported the accuracy and standard deviations.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Unanswerable questions comprise 20% of total questions per session.
ledger.quote: Since each question has five choices, unanswerable questions were set to comprise 20% of the total to fairly stratify the correct answers.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The Big Bang Theory: 805 sessions, average 1196.9 question candidates per session (1011.0 answerable / 185.9 unanswerable), 367,636 total tokens.
ledger.quote: The Big Bang Theory: Total Number of Tokens 367636, Total Number of Sessions 805, Average Question Candidates per Session 1196.9 (1011.0 / 185.9)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Dialogue average length is ~350k tokens, described as the longest among existing long-term dialogue datasets.
ledger.quote: DialSim includes multi-party dialogues with an average length of 350k tokens, making it the longest among existing long-term dialogue datasets.
ledger.locator: Section 1, Introduction, Evaluating Long-Term Multi-Party Dialogue Understanding bullet
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: All baselines scored below 40% accuracy, indicating poor LLM performance on the benchmark.
ledger.quote: the performances of all baselines were below 40%, suggesting that current LLMs function poorly as conversational agents for multi-party long-term complex dialogues.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Oracle upper bound: Claude-3 Opus achieved 69.64% accuracy without time limit, exceeding best RAG-based method by 23.21%.
ledger.quote: Claude-3 Opus achieved the best performance of 69.64% in a setting with unlimited time, highlighting the challenging nature of our task. This result surpasses the best RAG-based method, Session Entire-BM25 setting, by 23.21%.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Fan quiz-based questions are easier than TKG-based questions: Mixtral scored 53.75% vs 41.14%; one-hop TKG 54.46% vs two-hop 17.92%.
ledger.quote: comparing the performance of fan quiz-based questions and TKG-based questions, the results were 53.75% and 41.14% respectively... one-hop questions had a performance of 54.46%, whereas two-hop questions had a performance of 17.92%
ledger.locator: Section 4.3, Error Analysis by Question Type
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Adversarial name modification caused 5–10% performance drop under unlimited time conditions.
ledger.quote: when we experimented under unlimited time conditions, performance dropped by 5% to 10%.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Scripts sourced from 5 consecutive seasons per TV show downloaded from Kaggle; fan quizzes from FunTrivia.
ledger.quote: DialSim was developed using scripts from five consecutive seasons of popular TV shows (i.e., Friends, The Big Bang Theory, and The Office). The scripts were downloaded from the website Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: TKG uses 32 relations derived from DialogRE; triples extracted by ChatGPT-4 and manually verified by authors.
ledger.quote: We employed 32 relations (e.g., girlfriend) derived from DialogRE... These triples were then refined by the authors.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Dataset released under MIT License via GitHub and HuggingFace.
ledger.quote: The dataset is released under MIT License... The dataset and the code will be released at https://github.com/jiho283/Simulator.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: No recommended train/dev/test splits exist for DialSim.
ledger.quote: Are there recommended data splits (e.g., training, development/validation, testing)? N/A.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The simulator is claimed to be the first work evaluating conversational agent performance in a time-constrained environment.
ledger.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that evaluates the performance of a conversational agent in a time-constrained environment.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: 30% of questions per simulation run are drawn from fan quiz pool to balance fan quiz vs TKG question proportions.
ledger.quote: The number of questions based on fan quizzes was significantly smaller than the questions based on the TKG. Thus, 30% of the questions were intentionally extracted from the fan quiz-based during the simulation.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The agent must distinguish between known and unknown information, implying abstention or unanswerable question handling is evaluated.
ledger.quote: requiring it to respond to spontaneous questions using past dialogue information and to distinguish between known and unknown information
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: v1.0 is the dataset version described in the paper; v1.1 adds unanswerable multi-hop questions.
ledger.quote: v1.0: This version includes the dataset as described in the paper. v1.1: To incorporate more diverse and challenging data, this version has been updated to include unanswerable multi-hop questions.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Scoring for multi_choice_unstructured and open_ended formats is performed by GPT-4o-mini as an LLM judge.
ledger.quote: we use gpt-4o-mini as a judge when answer_format is "multi_choice_unstructured" or "open_ended"
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Oracle retrieval is available as a retrieval setting, enabling upper-bound retrieval experiments.
ledger.quote: ret_method : Retrieval method, default is "bm25". Options include "openai-emb", "bm25", "no_ret", and "oracle".
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: The benchmark tests agents on three TV show corpora: Friends, The Big Bang Theory, and The Office.
ledger.quote: script_name : TV show script for the simulation, default is "friends". Options include "friends", "bigbang", and "theoffice".
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: An adversarial evaluation mode shuffles or replaces character names to test robustness.
ledger.quote: name_shuffle : Type of adversarial test, default is "original". Options include "original", "shuffle", and "new_name". "shuffle" means an adversarial setting, and "new_name" means placing generic names.
